record: CR-01C3A -- Composite Parent Registration Feasibility. Can MiseryRuntime publish a Runtime-owned UDataTable<S_ItemDetails> as an additional parent of MasterItemList instead of writing every mod row into vanilla ItemList?
verdict: FEASIBLE IN PRINCIPLE, WITH ONE UNPROVEN WRITE. There is NO engine-native reachable API for changing the parent set, so attaching requires one direct write to MasterItemList.ParentTables. Everything else in the chain is engine-native and derivable. Preferred production architecture = B (one Runtime aggregate parent table); fallback = C (direct ItemList mutation, already proven).

session.note: a second, independent game session from the one CR-01C3 preconditions were read in

0_eventgraphfunction_unknown_closed.question: Is UFunction::EventGraphFunction non-null for AddItem, which would make ProcessEvent discard our Parms buffer (ScriptCore.cpp:2041-2049)?
0_eventgraphfunction_unknown_closed.answer: NO. AddItem->EventGraphFunction == nullptr. No STOP required.
0_eventgraphfunction_unknown_closed.layout_derivation: UFunction after UStruct(0xB0): 0xB0 FunctionFlags, 0xB4 NumParms, 0xB6 ParmsSize, 0xB8 ReturnValueOffset, 0xBA RPCId, 0xBC RPCResponseId, 0xC0 FirstPropertyToInit, 0xC8 EventGraphFunction, 0xD0 EventGraphCallOffset, 0xD8 Func (Class.h:1789-1830)

how_the_offset_was_PROVEN_rather_than_as.problem: +0xC8 is null for ALL 17032 live UFunctions, so no positive control for the field exists in this build and 'always zero' is also what wrong-offset padding looks like.
how_the_offset_was_PROVEN_rather_than_as.discriminator: If UE_BLUEPRINT_EVENTGRAPH_FASTCALLS were absent from the layout, Func would sit at +0xC8 and would be a .text pointer everywhere. Observed instead: +0xC8 null 17032/17032, and +0xD8 a .text pointer 17031/17032, with a single value (RVA 0x12ac660) shared by 6616 functions -- the UObject::ProcessInternal thunk every Blueprint function points at. Func is therefore at 0xD8, which forces the EventGraphFunction/EventGraphCallOffset pair to occupy 0xC8/0xD0.
how_the_offset_was_PROVEN_rather_than_as.second_line: +0xC0 behaves exactly like FirstPropertyToInit: non-null for 1237 functions, and every single one of those 1237 also carries FUNC_HasDefaults (zero counterexamples). The converse correctly does not hold (1816 HasDefaults with a null pointer), because FirstPropertyToInit tracks local struct properties with defaults, a subset.
how_the_offset_was_PROVEN_rather_than_as.why_it_is_null_everywhere: the compiler sets it only for a simple no-parameter stub graph whose ubergraph has FirstPropertyToInit == nullptr AND PostConstructLink == nullptr (KismetCompilerVMBackend.cpp:1266-1276). ExecuteUbergraph_BP_MasterInventory has FirstPropertyToInit non-null, so no stub in that class qualifies -- which is exactly why the no-parameter stub SGK UpdateAllAttachments also reads null. The observation is explained, not merely recorded.
how_the_offset_was_PROVEN_rather_than_as.corroboration: RVA 0x12ac660 sits 0x470 past the independently proven ProcessEvent at RVA 0x12ac1f0 -- same translation unit (ScriptCore.cpp), consistent with ProcessInternal.

1_masteritemlist_parent_model_OBSERVED.ParentTables: reflected FArrayProperty at offset 176, TArray<TObjectPtr<UDataTable>>, live Data=0x15a36c5d530 Num=1 Max=2 -- one element of SPARE CAPACITY
1_masteritemlist_parent_model_OBSERVED.OldParentTables: reflected FArrayProperty at offset 192, a SEPARATE allocation (Data=0x15a5c1d6460, Num=1, Max=2). Transient. The difference between the two arrays is what drives delegate subscribe/unsubscribe.

1_masteritemlist_parent_model_OBSERVED.all_seven_composites: MasterItemList 496, MasterBuildPartList 210, MasterCookingList 15, MasterCraftingRecipeList 104, MasterDeviceList 18, MasterGridLayoutList 1, MasterSpawnerList 251 -- each has exactly one parent and each ParentTables array is Num=1 Max=2
1_masteritemlist_parent_model_OBSERVED.RowStruct_identity: MasterItemList->RowStruct and ItemList->RowStruct are the SAME UScriptStruct pointer (0x15a0b2b3100). A runtime table only has to copy that pointer.

2_parent_mutation_api_VERDICT.engine_api: UCompositeDataTable::AppendParentTables, RemoveParentTables, AddParentTable, RemoveParentTable (CompositeDataTable.h, bodies at CompositeDataTable.cpp:276-313)
why: they are plain non-virtual ENGINE_API members -- not in any vtable, so no slot can be derived

they carry no UFUNCTION macro. Confirmed LIVE: walking the children chain of both /Script/Engine.DataTable and /Script/Engine.CompositeDataTable returns ZERO UFunctions, so there is no ProcessEvent route either
no export table exists in a monolithic Shipping build, and their RVAs are not derivable read-only from anything observed

additionally, nothing inside the engine calls them -- they exist for game C++ -- so a monolithic link may well have dropped them entirely. Unverifiable, and moot, since they are unreachable regardless
2_parent_mutation_api_VERDICT.conclusion: There is NO provable engine-native path equivalent to changing the parent table set. Attaching a parent requires writing MasterItemList.ParentTables directly. This is the single unproven write in the whole candidate and it is what the next gate must decide.

3_delegate_and_rebuild_semantics_OBSERVE.subscription: UCompositeDataTable::OnParentTablesUpdated (CompositeDataTable.cpp:315-345) does, in order: (a) unsubscribe from every table in OldParentTables that is no longer in ParentTables (:324-330); (b) UpdateCachedRowMap (:332); (c) subscribe to every table in ParentTables that was not in OldParentTables (:334-341); (d) OldParentTables = ParentTables (:343). A bUpdatingParentTables guard prevents recursion (:317-322).
3_delegate_and_rebuild_semantics_OBSERVE.rebuild: UpdateCachedRowMap (:53-142) runs FindLoops, then UDataTable::EmptyTable() (:87) which DestroyStructs and frees every cached row, then re-adds every parent's rows in ParentTables order with an explicitly qualified UDataTable::AddRow (:118). A parent whose RowStruct != the composite's RowStruct is SKIPPED with an error log (:96-107) -- a natural fail-closed guard.
3_delegate_and_rebuild_semantics_OBSERVE.trigger: UDataTable::AddRow / RemoveRow open DATATABLE_CHANGE_SCOPE (DataTable.cpp:456, :435); the scope destructor calls HandleDataTableChanged when the refcount reaches 0 (:53-63); that ends in OnDataTableChanged().Broadcast() (:230). None of it is editor-gated (DataTable.h:176, :180, :186).
3_delegate_and_rebuild_semantics_OBSERVE.LIVE_CONFIRMATION_in_this_second_session: ItemList's OnDataTableChanged invocation list (offset 0x98) holds Num=1; MasterItemList's own holds Num=0. Independently reproduced from the earlier session, in a different process instance.
3_delegate_and_rebuild_semantics_OBSERVE.delegate_offset_now_bounded_EXACTLY: the reflected properties pin it: ImportKeyField is at 136 (0x88, 16 bytes, ending 0x98) and the subclass's first member ParentTables is at 176 (0xB0). That leaves exactly 0x18 = 24 bytes at 0x98 -- precisely sizeof(FMulticastDelegateBase) (TArray InvocationList 16 + two int32). The structural derivation and the observed content agree.
3_delegate_and_rebuild_semantics_OBSERVE.data_neutral_publication_trigger: UDataTable::RemoveRow(<a name that does not exist>) on ItemList is data-neutral: RemoveRowInternal calls RowMap.RemoveAndCopyValue, which leaves RowData null for a missing key, so nothing is destroyed or freed (DataTable.cpp:433-451). The ONLY effect is the scope destructor's broadcast. That single call publishes a newly appended parent AND subscribes it, entirely inside engine code.

4_duplicate_precedence_and_cycles.precedence: 'Tables with higher indices override data in tables with lower indices' (CompositeDataTable.h, above ParentTables). Mechanically: UpdateCachedRowMap iterates ParentTables in order and calls UDataTable::AddRow, which removes an existing row of that name first (DataTable.cpp:461) -- so the LAST parent to supply a name wins. Appending our table at the end therefore gives mod rows precedence over vanilla.
4_duplicate_precedence_and_cycles.crucially_non_destructive: that precedence lives entirely in the composite's CACHE. The vanilla ItemList row is never written, and it reappears verbatim the moment our table is detached and the composite rebuilds.
4_duplicate_precedence_and_cycles.cycles: UCompositeDataTable::FindLoops (called first inside UpdateCachedRowMap, :55) walks the parent graph and leaves the table empty if a cycle exists. Our table would be a plain UDataTable, not a composite, so it cannot participate in a cycle at all.
4_duplicate_precedence_and_cycles.row_struct_mismatch: a parent whose RowStruct pointer differs is skipped, not merged -- so getting RowStruct wrong degrades to 'our rows are absent', never to corruption.

construction.path: UGameplayStatics::SpawnObject, live @0x15a380fdec0, FunctionFlags 0x4022403 = Native|Static|Final|Public|RequiredAPI|BlueprintCallable, ParmsSize 24: (TSubclassOf<UObject> ObjectClass @0, UObject* Outer @8) -> UObject* ReturnValue @16
construction.implementation: returns NewObject<UObject>(Outer, ObjectClass, NAME_None, RF_StrongRefOnFrame) after three null/ClassWithin guards (GameplayStatics.cpp:813-833)
construction.verdict: FEASIBLE and engine-native -- no StaticConstructObject_Internal RVA is needed. The UDataTable UClass is live at /Script/Engine.DataTable.
construction.caveat_RF_StrongRefOnFrame: the returned object is kept alive only by the script frame. It MUST be rooted immediately through the CR-01A engine root path (SetRootFlags/GRoots) in the same GameThread job, or it is collectable as soon as the frame unwinds.
construction.outer: UDataTable declares no Within, so ClassWithin is UObject and any live UObject is an acceptable Outer. Choosing one that is not a vanilla content package is preferable; not yet decided.

row_struct_assignment.mechanism: UDataTable::RowStruct is a reflected FObjectProperty at offset 40. Writing it on an object WE created is not vanilla mutation. CPF_EditConst restricts the editor UI only.
row_struct_assignment.value: the exact same UScriptStruct pointer MasterItemList->RowStruct holds -- read live, never constructed or guessed

detached_population.mechanism: our table is a plain UDataTable, so its vtable slot 95 is the real UDataTable::AddRow at RVA 0x3548190 -- the exact primitive proven in CR-01C1 and CR-01C2R, applied to an object we own
detached_population.materializer: the CR-01C2R Route C materializer works unchanged: FMemory::Malloc(PropertiesSize) -> InitializeStruct (struct vtable slot 96) -> populate verified value types -> AddRow -> DestroyStruct (slot 97) + FMemory::Free
detached_population.no_rebuild_while_detached: the composite only rebuilds on a broadcast from a table it is SUBSCRIBED to. While our table is not yet in ParentTables, nothing is subscribed to it, so populating N rows costs ZERO composite rebuilds.
detached_population.GetEmptyUsingStruct: uses RowStruct when set, and only falls back to FTableRowBase with an error log when it is null (DataTable.cpp:400-413). Setting RowStruct before the first AddRow is therefore both necessary and sufficient.
detached_population.status: mechanism proven; not yet exercised on a runtime-created table.

A_one_parent_table_per_mod.vanilla_preservation: vanilla ItemList RowMap never written; MasterItemList.ParentTables written once PER MOD
A_one_parent_table_per_mod.composite_rebuilds: 1 if all appends are batched before a single trigger; otherwise 1 per mod, and 1 per mod hot-reload
A_one_parent_table_per_mod.row_pointer_invalidation: proportional to the number of rebuilds
A_one_parent_table_per_mod.multi_mod_determinism: WEAK. Conflicts are resolved implicitly by ParentTables index, i.e. by load order, with no explicit arbitration and nothing to audit.
A_one_parent_table_per_mod.rollback: remove one element per mod and re-trigger; index bookkeeping grows with mod count
A_one_parent_table_per_mod.collision: non-destructive -- a colliding name only shadows in the cache
A_one_parent_table_per_mod.capacity: needs N spare slots in a vanilla array that currently has 1
A_one_parent_table_per_mod.verdict: rejected: same unproven write as B, but with worse determinism and N times the array bookkeeping

B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.vanilla_preservation: vanilla ItemList RowMap NEVER written. Exactly ONE vanilla field is ever touched: MasterItemList.ParentTables, Num 1 -> 2, using the spare capacity that already exists.
B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.composite_rebuilds: ONE, at publication. All N mod rows are added while detached.
B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.row_pointer_invalidation: one rebuild's worth, once -- the minimum any approach can achieve
B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.multi_mod_determinism: STRONG. The Runtime arbitrates Mod A/B/C itself and publishes one already-resolved table, so precedence is explicit, auditable and independent of load order.
B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.rollback: write Num back to 1, fire the data-neutral trigger, unroot our table. The composite returns to bit-for-bit vanilla content.
B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.collision: non-destructive. A mod row named like a vanilla row SHADOWS it in the cache; the vanilla ItemList row is untouched and returns on detach.
B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.ownership: our table is Runtime-owned and rooted via the CR-01A engine root path; once attached it is ALSO traced by GC through MasterItemList.ParentTables (a UPROPERTY). Two independent keep-alive paths.
B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.multiplayer: best positioned -- one deterministic published artifact that can be hashed and version-checked between client and server. Still UNKNOWN in substance.
B_one_runtime_aggregate_parent_table.blocking_gap: the ParentTables append is a direct write into a vanilla UObject's array, because the engine's own parent API is unreachable. This is the one thing that is not engine-native.

C_direct_ItemList_mutation.vanilla_preservation: vanilla ROWS are provably preserved (all 496 hash-identical across CR-01C1 and CR-01C2R), but the vanilla table's RowMap gains keys
C_direct_ItemList_mutation.composite_rebuilds: ONE PER REGISTERED ROW. N rows means N full 496-row destroy-and-deep-copy cycles, roughly 1.1 MB of churn each.
C_direct_ItemList_mutation.multi_mod_determinism: WEAK and silent. Last writer wins with no arbitration point.
C_direct_ItemList_mutation.rollback: RemoveRow per name -- clean, EXCEPT after a collision
C_direct_ItemList_mutation.collision: DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. UDataTable::AddRow calls RemoveRowInternal first (DataTable.cpp:461), which DestroyStructs and frees the existing row. A mod that reuses a vanilla row name permanently deletes that vanilla item for the session, and the Runtime cannot restore it.
C_direct_ItemList_mutation.ownership: the engine owns every row end to end; the Runtime allocates and frees nothing
C_direct_ItemList_mutation.status: FULLY PROVEN TODAY, end to end, twice
C_direct_ItemList_mutation.verdict: kept as the fallback precisely because it is the only fully proven option, but it is not the right production shape

7_decision.preferred: B -- one Runtime-owned aggregate parent table (working name MBPL_EffectiveModItems), attached once to MasterItemList.ParentTables after being fully populated while detached
7_decision.fallback: C -- direct additive registration into vanilla ItemList with the already-proven engine AddRow/RemoveRow
7_decision.decisive_reason: collision safety. Under C a third-party mod that reuses a vanilla row name irreversibly destroys that vanilla row; under B the same name merely shadows it and the vanilla row returns on detach. On a platform that must survive arbitrary third-party content that difference is categorical, and it is reinforced by 1 rebuild instead of N and by explicit rather than load-order-dependent multi-mod precedence.
7_decision.honest_cost_of_B: B trades 'only engine code ever writes vanilla data' (which C satisfies completely) for one 8-byte pointer write plus one int32 Num increment in a vanilla object's array. That trade has NOT been authorised and is exactly what the next gate must decide.
7_decision.CR-01C1_and_CR-01C2R_remain_valid: unchanged and unaffected. B uses the SAME primitives -- engine UDataTable::AddRow/RemoveRow and the Route C materializer -- merely pointed at a table the Runtime owns instead of a vanilla one.

8_what_B_still_needs_proven: constructing a UDataTable at runtime through the reflected UGameplayStatics::SpawnObject and rooting it in the same GameThread job before the script frame unwinds
assigning RowStruct to the exact live S_ItemDetails pointer and confirming AddRow then allocates 2264-byte rows
populating it while detached and confirming ZERO composite rebuilds occur

the ParentTables append itself: whether spare capacity exists (Max-Num >= 1 must be re-checked at run time and fail closed if not; growing the array would require engine-allocator TArray semantics we have not derived)
that a data-neutral RemoveRow of a non-existent name on ItemList does publish and subscribe the new parent, and changes nothing else
clean detach: Num back to 1, rebuild, and MasterItemList's 496 rows hash-identical to the pre-attach baseline
9_remaining_unknowns: Whether any NATIVE code caches a raw MasterItemList row pointer across frames; every rebuild invalidates all of them.
Whether AppendParentTables et al. survive the monolithic link at all -- unverifiable read-only, and moot because they are unreachable either way.
The RVA of FScopedDataTableChange's constructor, which would let many registrations share one rebuild without the detach/attach dance.
Whether an attached parent survives save/load or a level change -- BLOCKED ON M4 LIFECYCLE EVIDENCE.
